title: Chris: replace or retain, with the tenure asymmetry (Boudreau & Berger)
story: Chris is slightly above average (+0.1 SD) and has survived the risky first year, so their expected remaining tenure is 4 years (range 2 to 7). The manager wants to replace Chris with a candidate they rate +0.6 SD (range 0.2 to 1.0). A naive model gives both 3 years and says replace, by 5,000. Correcting the replacement's tenure for the first-year exit hazard (shaving 25%: 3 -> 2.25 years) and using Chris's survivorship-adjusted tenure, retaining wins by 6,000. SDy is 20k a year; replacing costs 25k.
source: Marritt, 'Should you replace Sam?': the replace-or-retain condition (r_rep x T_rep - r_inc x T_inc) x SDy > C, after Boudreau & Berger (1985)
what_it_tests: the Boudreau-Berger condition as a two-option tree with formula numbers
naive vs tenure-corrected answers disagreeing (a calculated number holds the naive answer)
switch points on fixed and ranged numbers, inside and outside their ranges
two ranges multiplying each other in one option
note: Both tenure corrections run against the replacement only because Chris is above average (r_inc > 0). For a below-average incumbent (r_inc < 0) a longer incumbent tenure makes replacing more attractive, not less; the article states the two adjustments 'both run against the replacement' without that condition.
